gary_2026_09_26_the_harness_engg_model_w.summary: Gary's Guide: MongoDB's next chapter of agentic infrastructure is memory, persistence, & self-evolving systems. Join us for a hackathon with the MongoDB, as well as our supporting partners - AWS, OpenAI, Fireworks, Vercel, Openrouter, ElevenLabs - focused on solving the hardest problem in agentic AI: building harnesses that can adapt, remember, & operate reliably over the long haul. We're looking for impactful projects built with MongoDB Atlas, Vector Search, & Agentic Memory tooling. Whether you're building agents that rewrite their own guardrails, systems that hold context across weeks-long tasks, or entirely new approaches to persistent agent memory, this is your opportunity to build the infrastructure the next generation of agents will run on. Top judges from across MongoDB's ecosystem will be joining us, & prizes will be announced soon. Note: This event is fully in-person in NYC. Space is limited. Maximum team size is four. All attendees must submit an application & be approved to attend. If selected as a finalist we require one person from your team to record a demo on-site September 26th which will then be displayed at .local NYC. To be eligible to win, finalists must also be available on September 30th to attend MongoDB.local NYC & present their project.

gary_2026_09_26_pmai_vibe_coding_worksho.summary: Gary's Guide: Curious about coding with AI? This is the perfect place to start. If you are a: Non-technical founder/operator SME who wants to incorporate AI Someone who feel left behind by AI Aspiring builders/students Working professionals looking to 10x productivity Generally curious about agentic AI You have to come! In this beginner-friendly workshop, we'll walk you through everything you need to go from zero to building with Codex from Open AI, among with other tools. We cover: Understanding the basics of how the tools work as an agentic coding assistant in your terminal Building a real project from scratch using natural language commands Learning how to prompt effectively so the AI tools do what you actually want No prior experience with AI coding tools is required, just bring your laptop! Participants are responsible for their own subscriptions. By the end of this session, you'll have a working project & the confidence to keep building on your own. About Narra Collective: Narra Collective is a community-driven coworking & flex workspace in Jersey City serving founders, small business owners, & corporate teams. Part of the less than 1% of coworking spaces in the U.S. that are both women- & minority-owned, Narra brings a perspective shaped by lived experience, building spaces where access, connection, & opportunity are intentionally created. Through thoughtfully designed space & programming, Narra facilitates meaningful relationships, knowledge exchange, & business growth within a highly engaged local ecosystem. About Pioneering Minds AI: At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

gary_2026_10_07_pmai_creativity_business.title: PMAI - Creativity & Business Problems In Age Of AI
gary_2026_10_07_pmai_creativity_business.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_10_07_pmai_creativity_business.summary: Gary's Guide: Creativity & Business Problems in the Age of AI - a workshop for entrepreneurs We are entering a strange moment for creativity. For decades, we have been taught that innovation comes from thinking outside the box, brainstorming more ideas, & waiting for that breakthrough moment. But in the age of AI, & ideas are suddenly abundant, the real challenge is no longer simply coming up with more ideas. It is knowing how to find the right pieces, make unexpected connections, & turn them into something genuinely new & useful. This hands-on workshop, led by our head of program Jeffrey, introduces a practical methodology for doing exactly that. What we'll cover We'll start by looking at some of the traditional assumptions behind creativity & innovation: brainstorming, originality, intuition, & the idea of the lone creative genius, & why some of those assumptions are becoming less useful in an AI-native world. We'll then introduce a different way to approach creative problem-solving: instead of trying to invent the answer from scratch, you'll learn how to break a problem apart, deliberately search for useful precedents & ideas, & recombine existing elements in new ways. Through real-world case studies, we'll examine how successful products, businesses, & innovations often emerge not from a completely original idea, but from making the right connection between things that already exist. Most importantly, this will not be a lecture. You'll work through the methodology yourself, apply it to actual business problems, & leave with a framework you can reuse when thinking about products, positioning, growth, operations, or your next startup idea. Who should attend This workshop is designed primarily for: Early-stage founders, aspiring entrepreneurs, small business owners, product builders, & operators who regularly need to solve ambiguous problems with limited resources. No technical background is required. If you have ever stared at a blank page thinking, I need a better idea, this workshop is for you. Come with a problem. Leave with a different way of thinking about it.

jc_culture_10004823_2026_09_25_the_socie.title: The Society of American Graphic Artists (SAGA) 91st Annual Members Exhibition 2026
jc_culture_10004823_2026_09_25_the_socie.label: Art / Culture
jc_culture_10004823_2026_09_25_the_socie.place: MANA CONTEMPORARY, 888 NEWARK AVE., JERSEY CITY
jc_culture_10004823_2026_09_25_the_socie.summary: 91st Annual Members Exhibition The Society of American Graphic Artists (SAGA) is excited to announce its upcoming 91st Annual Members Exhibition, to be held at Mana Contemporary in Jersey City from September 11–27, 2026 (Fridays and Saturdays, 3:00–7:00 PM; Sundays, 12:00–3:00 PM). The exhibition will feature 200 hand-pulled prints representing a broad range of printmaking techniques and subjects, created by SAGA artists from across the country. Awards will be juried by Leslie Diuguid, founder of Du-Good Press in Brooklyn. The Society of American Graphic Artists (SAGA) is a nonprofit organization established in 1915 whose mission is to promote contemporary printmakers, cultivate printmaking appreciation and education, and provide a collaborative and inclusive platform for artists across the country. https://sagaprints.com/ Hosting this year’s exhibition is Monira Foundation, an independent nonprofit institution that functions as a radical experimental laboratory, working in close collaboration with artists, curators, musicians, dancers, producers, and writers to conceive, realize, and present innovative projects in all media. Monira is located within Mana Contemporary, a 2-million-square-foot art center. The complex occupies a renovated 100-year-old former tobacco warehouse, featuring expansive exhibition spaces, working artist studios, the International Center of Photography archives, and more. A free public reception and awards ceremony with participating artists will be held on Saturday, September 26, from 3:00–5:00 PM. Guests are invited to enjoy light refreshments while celebrating the diversity and innovation of contemporary printmaking. WHEN Exhibition: Fridays–Sundays, September 11–27, 2026 Public Reception & Awards Ceremony: Saturday, September 26, 2026 3:00–5:00 PM WHERE Mana Contemporary 888 Newark Avenue Jersey City, NJ 07306

jc_culture_10004828_2026_09_25_rent_the_.label: Music / Movies
jc_culture_10004828_2026_09_25_rent_the_.place: ART HOUSE, 345 MARIN BLVD, JERSEY CITY
jc_culture_10004828_2026_09_25_rent_the_.summary: Experience the groundbreaking Tony Award-winning musical and Pulitzer Prize-winning drama that defined a generation. Presented at Art House Productions during the 30th anniversary year of its original premiere, RENT follows a vibrant community of artists, musicians, and dreamers in New York City’s East Village as they pursue their passions, navigate love and loss, and strive to make a meaningful impact on the world around them. Set against the backdrop of the AIDS crisis, poverty, addiction, economic uncertainty, and a rapidly changing city, these artists discover the power of friendship, the importance of creative expression, and the enduring strength of community. Featuring iconic songs and an unforgettable rock score, RENT celebrates resilience, human connection, and the transformative role of the arts in times of hardship. This production is especially meaningful as part of Art House Productions’ 25th Anniversary Season. Founded in the wake of September 11, 2001, Art House was created to bring people together through the arts during a time of profound loss and uncertainty. Thirty years after its premiere, RENT remains as relevant, timeless, and inspiring as ever, reminding us all to measure our lives in love.

jc_culture_10003570_2026_09_30_hamilton_.summary: Join us at the Hamilton Park Farmers Market, your midweek destination for fresh, local, and thoughtfully crafted food and goods. Each week, we’re proud to feature farm-fresh produce from Stony Hill Farm alongside a curated selection of specialty vendors. Browse a variety of offerings including our long time vendor Pickles and Olives, fresh seafood from Scale Fish Market, and prepared foods perfect for dinner. You can also find baked goods, candles, personal care products, and more. You can even take advantage of convenient services like on-site knife sharpening while you shop. On the first and second Wednesdays of each month, enjoy live entertainment that adds to the vibrant, community atmosphere of the market. Whether you’re shopping for the week, grabbing a bite, or simply enjoying the park, the Hamilton Park Farmers Market is a welcoming space to connect with local vendors and neighbors.

jc_culture_44040_2026_10_03_free_diapers.summary: Please Take Our Ad: Community Giving Luvs is bringing its Give Back Billboard to Jersey City, turning an advertisement into an opportunity to directly support local families with free diapers. From 12–6 p.m., families can visit Mary McLeod Bethune Park and take part in an interactive billboard made from Luvs diaper packs. As the packs are removed, the billboard will gradually reveal the message: “Leak protection shouldn’t be a luxury.” For 50 years, Luvs has stood for value, and as families face the rising cost of raising children, the brand is bringing that commitment directly to the community through free diapers, giveaways and more. One free box of diapers per household, while supplies last. Sizes subject to availability. No purchase necessary.

jc_culture_10004837_2026_10_08_rent_the_.title: RENT: The Musical
jc_culture_10004837_2026_10_08_rent_the_.label: Music / Movies
jc_culture_10004837_2026_10_08_rent_the_.place: ART HOUSE, 345 MARIN BLVD, JERSEY CITY
jc_culture_10004837_2026_10_08_rent_the_.summary: Experience the groundbreaking Tony Award-winning musical and Pulitzer Prize-winning drama that defined a generation. Presented at Art House Productions during the 30th anniversary year of its original premiere, RENT follows a vibrant community of artists, musicians, and dreamers in New York City’s East Village as they pursue their passions, navigate love and loss, and strive to make a meaningful impact on the world around them. Set against the backdrop of the AIDS crisis, poverty, addiction, economic uncertainty, and a rapidly changing city, these artists discover the power of friendship, the importance of creative expression, and the enduring strength of community. Featuring iconic songs and an unforgettable rock score, RENT celebrates resilience, human connection, and the transformative role of the arts in times of hardship. This production is especially meaningful as part of Art House Productions’ 25th Anniversary Season. Founded in the wake of September 11, 2001, Art House was created to bring people together through the arts during a time of profound loss and uncertainty. Thirty years after its premiere, RENT remains as relevant, timeless, and inspiring as ever, reminding us all to measure our lives in love.
